figure_images.alt: Five spike marks share a time axis with an activation trace. Each mark aligns with a vertical rise of one activation unit. The activation decays smoothly between spikes, and nearby spikes build on the remaining activation.

A line of fixed points lies at y equals zero. An imposed vertical jump from zero zero to zero two is followed by a straight tilted flow toward one zero. Equal time marks crowd toward the endpoint. Perpendicular projection would return to zero zero and miss the lasting shift of one. The tangent is one zero; the left vector measures delta x plus one half delta y.

As theta increases through the interior from minus 20 to 20 activation units, r1 increases toward 200 spikes per second and r2 decreases toward zero. Their dashed sum stays at 200. A lower aligned plot shows D constant at 100 coordinate units squared per second. Open endpoint circles exclude both boundaries.

Wrapped Gaussian densities at 0.2, 1 and 5 seconds broaden toward a dashed uniform density over angular errors from minus pi to pi. Below, line mean squared error rises linearly while wrapped angular mean squared error approaches a horizontal pi squared over three reference, with the same constant diffusion coefficient.
